why: It now also removes 'wh-check-' + id, the same key ckKey() writes for that list ('wh-check-' + cur.army), next to 'wh-used-' + id. render.js sets both keys before Remove and checks that both are null afterwards. The fold-open keys ('ck|id|…' in openStrats) live only for the session, so they need no clearing. Imported lists get an id no other list has, so a later import cannot inherit old boxes.

The mechanics are right. Every fold starts closed (checked on 5 lists), and a fold stays open for the session. There are no stratagems. Once-per-battle lines reuse the Overview's own boxes: ticks('r:'+name), the 'r:'+name+':'+row rows for Kindred Sorcery, abilityTicks and copyKey, all in wh-used. So the two screens stay in sync, and Reset (which writes only wh-check) cannot clear them; Undo restores the list. Three points need the owner's call. (1) An item counted as triggered by its words, but whose entry has only u, is placed under ACTIVE NOW, not TO DO NOW or When unclear. Examples: Wrath of Khorne ('When … is selected to fight, … can have: [CLEAVE 1]. Or: +1 AP'), Crush All Who Stand Before Us ('Each time this model’s unit is selected to fight, you can use this ability'), Direct the Slaughter and Overwhelming Wrath. Their trigger moment is not read, and owner rule 2 says such items belong under When unclear. The screen instead files them as in force. (2) Try Dat Button!'s dice results '1–2', '3–4' and '5–6' appear as three TO DO NOW lines in Shooting · Your turn and in both Fight phases. They are results of the rule's roll, not things to do. (3) The bottom note says ACTIVE NOW means what a trigger puts in force (riled up), but it also holds each item's own used-in phases (Blood Tithe's options, Doom, Executioner). Separately: if the ckTriggered fix is taken, the option filter here must become `if(!trig && !ckTriggered(o, r, o.n)) continue;` so that Magna Imperator's Additional Effect stays listed (tested in a scratch copy). Minor: the tick id of an ability group ('a:'+name+'|'+hash) leaves out the na flag that the group key includes. So the same ability on a usable unit and an unusable unit would share boxes within a section.

It tests the whole text, including the options' words. So an always-on rule counts as triggered because one of its options is. Magna Imperator ('When a friendly ADEPTUS CUSTODES unit is selected to attack, that unit’s attacks can: Re-roll one hit roll …') is listed as ACTIVE NOW in Movement · Their turn, Shooting · Your turn and both Fight phases. The only reason is its option '**Additional Effect:** You can select one enemy MONSTER/VEHICLE unit …'. The same happens to Higher Imperatives ('Friendly NORN EMISSARY/NORN ASSIMILATOR units have the following ability'), which lands under When unclear even though its Protean Purpose is already listed with the units. The fix tests a rule's own lines without its options' lines, or the whole text when it is nothing but options (Icon of War). With an opt argument it tests one option's own words. Tested in a scratch copy: Magna Imperator and Higher Imperatives leave the screen, Additional Effect stays under When unclear, and Icon of War stays listed. render.js's own copy of `triggered`, and its option check (oIn), need the same change: unchanged, they report exactly 'Magna Imperator is not listed' and 'Higher Imperatives is not listed'. For the owner, not fixed here: abilities that only qualify by naming a phase, with no event and no choice, also count as triggered, because their derived t is set. Examples: Blitz Dem Gitz! ('In your Shooting phase, if this unit’s Blitzkannon weapon targets a unit …, that weapon has +6 A'), Finderz Keeperz ('In your Shooting phase, if any of the following apply, … +1 AP') and Deff from Above. Under owner rule 1 these read as always-on in that phase, yet they appear under TO DO NOW in Shooting · Your turn.

In order: an option's own trigger; else where it is used, with via (its rule's trigger), so a once-per-battle option is filed where it is chosen; else its rule's trigger; x goes to When unclear. Checked against the rule texts. Blood Tithe: Might of Khorne goes under TO DO NOW in both Command phases ('At the start of the Command phase, you can spend …'); Enraged Abjuration, Daemonic Rage and Boon of Blood go under ACTIVE NOW where used ('until the end of the battle'). Blessings of Khorne's options: Unbridled Bloodlust is active in both Charge phases, the other five in both Fight phases ('until the end of the battle round'). Martial Ka’tah's options: Calistus in Movement · Your turn, Salvus in Shooting · Your turn, and Dacatarai, Kaptaris and Rendax in both Fight phases ('Start of the Fight phase' / 'Fight phase' have no 'your', so either turn). Harbingers of Dread: Dismay is in Command · Their turn ('In the Battle-shock step of your opponent’s Command phase').

It takes table 1's used-in phases as they are, so phases the text rules out still show as ACTIVE NOW. Wreckin’ and Lootin’ ('In your Shooting phase, when a friendly BREAKA BOYZ/FLASH GITZ/TANKBUSTAS unit is selected to shoot, … that unit’s attacks can re-roll hit rolls of 1') gets u 'shooting:your,fight:either', so it is ACTIVE NOW in Fight · Your turn and Fight · Their turn (shooty). The fix: when the text names its trigger phases and states no duration, the use is limited to those phases and that turn. Both call sites pass the same withoutOptions text. Tested with derive --write in a scratch copy, the CHECKLIST changes only twice. Wreckin’ and Lootin’ becomes u 'shooting:your'. Knights of Legend loses u 'shooting:opp,fight:either', which came from its always-on 'Feel No Pain 6+'; its trigger, 'at the start of your Command phase … regains 1 lost wound', stays. Every other entry is unchanged: Dreadherder ('until the end of the turn'), Clever Know-wotz, Marked Prey and Moment Shackle keep their uses.

Checked against the texts. War Cry: 'If you do, friendly ORKS units with the Waaagh! ability are **riled up** until the end of the next turn'. The clause before 'are' has no if/while/unless/when, and riled up resolves to Waaagh! by alias, giving 'Riled up (War Cry) · Waaagh!'. Intimidating Motivation: '- Is **riled up** until the start of your next turn' resolves the same way. Even More Dakka and More Dakka ('If this unit is **riled up**'), and Dakka! Dakka! Dakka! ('While this unit is riled up'), are correctly skipped. The duration is read from the same sentence. Minor: DURATIONS 'turn' also matches a condition such as 'made a charge move this turn' if that sentence also puts a state in force. No current text does this.

The cases in the data are right. War Cry, from the Command phase in either turn with 'until the end of the next turn', covers the rest of that turn plus the whole other turn. From either side that is every phase of both turns, which matches its u. Intimidating Motivation, from Movement · Your turn with 'until the start of your next turn', gives Movement through Fight · Your turn plus the whole opponent's turn. That is u 'command:opp,movement:either,…', and Command · Your turn is correctly left out. Two cases were found by running the function directly. (1) A trigger 'at the end of your opponent’s turn' with 'until the end of the battle' gives only your turn's five phases, but to the end of the battle means every phase after it in both turns. (2) 'until the end of the phase' from the start of the battle round gives Command in both turns, but no phase is in progress at the start of the battle round, so per rule 2 that should be x. Neither case is in the current data, and the fixed function writes an identical CHECKLIST.

optionsOf drops worked examples from the options ('**Example:** …', Martial Ka’tah), so they stay in the rule's own words and table 1 reads them. Martial Ka’tah's example ('If you selected the Solar Watch detachment, … that unit has +2" M') gives it u 'movement:your'. So Martial Ka’tah shows as ACTIVE NOW in Movement · Your turn on lite-knights, which does not have Solar Watch. Its own words name only 'At the start of your Command phase'. Without the example line, timing() gives used {} (tested). With the fix, derive --write changes only that entry, to {"t":"command:your",…}.

fix.code: const withoutOptions = (text, table) => { const t = rulesText(text); return optionsOf(t, table).reduce((s2, o) => s2.replace(o.text, ''), t).replace(/^(?:- )?\*\*Examples?(?::\*\*|\*\*:).*$/gim, ''); };

why: When derive cannot place an item, ckStored turns the row's display phase tags (ph/turn) into TO DO NOW. Those tags show where the row appears, including where its effect is used, not when it triggers, so it guesses, against rule 2. Harbingers of Dread ('at the start of the first, third and fifth battle rounds, you can either select … or randomly select two Dread abilities') is under TO DO NOW at the Start of the battle round, and also in Command · Your turn and Command · Their turn (woof-woof, infernal-lance). That is the double filing ckEntry's atOnly exists to avoid. Icon of Khorne ('Each time you make a Blessings of Khorne roll, roll one additional D6 for each Bloodshed point you have') is under TO DO NOW at the Start of the battle round, and also in both Command phases, Movement · Their turn, Shooting · Your turn and both Fight phases (big-demons-baby, princes). Icon of War, whose text names no time, is under TO DO NOW in Command · Your turn, Movement · Their turn, both Shooting phases, Charge · Your turn and both Fight phases (purge-goes-the-foe). The fix keeps only the stored moment. Tested in a scratch copy: Harbingers and Icon of Khorne go only under the Start of the battle round, and Icon of War goes under When unclear with its options unchanged. render.js's checks pass (its want() skips stored items).

fix.code: const ckStored = (e, x) => e.x && x.at ? Object.assign({}, e, { x:0, at:x.at }) : e;
